Datasets

The canonical records every page on this site is rendered from, shown as they are written in data/*.json: one file and one record at a time, as a graph, a tree or the raw text. Read-only. Follow a reference to move from a record to the record it names.

Loading the explorer. Until it arrives — or without JavaScript — these are the 10 files it reads, each of which opens as it is written:

  • Instruments — data/instruments.json 38 in instruments, 37 in relationships
  • Institutions — data/institutions.json 21 in institutions
  • Enforcement — data/enforcement.json 21 in enforcement
  • Claims — data/claims.json 181 in claims
  • Sources — data/sources.json 223 in sources
  • Timeline — data/timeline.json 100 in events
  • Applicability rules — data/applicability.json 33 in rules
  • Glossary — data/glossary.json 15 in terms
  • Taxonomy — data/taxonomy.json 311 records in 35 collections
  • Brief structure — data/brief.json 13 in parts, 20 in reading_graph

How to read this view

Nesting is not a relationship. In the Structure view a solid line joins a card to an object or list written inside the same record. That is the shape of the file, and nothing more: it does not say that one legal instrument contains, amends or depends on another.

A reference is an id, and only an id. Records point at each other by holding another record’s id as a string. A value is shown as a reference only when it is exactly the id of a record in one of these files, and the field that holds it is named. The file records that the id is there; what the connection means is stated, where it is stated at all, in the records themselves — for instance in the summary of an interaction between instruments.

Derived facts are not in the files. A claim’s evidence grade, an enforcement record’s pipeline, an instrument’s competent authority and its key dates are computed when a page loads and are never stored. This view shows the files, so it shows none of them — except a claim’s grade, which is computed here by the same function the rest of the site uses and labelled as computed.

What a file does not say is not shown as a value. A field written as null is shown as null; a field a record does not have is not drawn. Neither is a finding that something does not exist. Each file’s own notes, shown beside its records, state what its fields mean.
